q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and ____.
e: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant ____.
e: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant composition. Composition is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pure substances are classified as either elements or ____.
e: Pure substances are classified as either elements or compounds. A compound contains two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. A pure substance has a fixed composition, either an element or a compound.

q: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and ____.
e: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and indivisible. Atoms can be split into protons, neutrons, and electrons, so they are not truly indivisible.

q: Today, the atom is still considered as the basic unit of any ____.
e: Today, the atom is still considered as the basic unit of any element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon ____.
e: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atoms are the smallest particles into which an element can be ____.
e: Atoms are the smallest particles into which an element can be divided. Divided is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined ____.
e: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state. State is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Substances like these, which cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means, are called ____.
e: Substances like these, which cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means, are called elements. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: On the basis of their properties, elements may be classified into two groups, metals and ____.
e: On the basis of their properties, elements may be classified into two groups, metals and non-metals. Non-metals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metals show metallic ____.
e: Metals show metallic luster. Luster is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ____.
e: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile. Ductile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metals are good conductors of heat and ____.
e: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Non-metals are usually ____.
e: Non-metals are usually brittle. Brittle is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and ____.
e: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The atoms of some elements are joined together in small groups called ____.
e: The atoms of some elements are joined together in small groups called molecules. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A molecule of an element (molecular element) consists of atoms of the ____ kind.
e: A molecule of an element (molecular element) consists of atoms of the same kind. Same is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A molecule of a compound (molecular compound) consists of more than one kind of ____.
e: A molecule of a compound (molecular compound) consists of more than one kind of atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The atoms of different elements in the molecule of a compound are combined in a definite ___.
e: The atoms of different elements in the molecule of a compound are combined in a definite ratio. A compound contains two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio.

q: Hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a ____ molecule.
e: Hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a diatomic molecule. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water is formed by combining two different elements: H and O, so it is a ____ molecule (binary compound).
e: Water is formed by combining two different elements: H and O, so it is a triatomic molecule (binary compound). Triatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In ammonia, there are more than three atoms from two different elements: N and H, so it is a ____ molecule (binary compound).
e: In ammonia, there are more than three atoms from two different elements: N and H, so it is a polyatomic molecule (binary compound). Polyatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In ethanol, there are more than three atoms from three different elements, so it is a polyatomic molecule ( compound).
e: In ethanol, there are more than three atoms from three different elements, so it is a polyatomic molecule (compound). Ternary is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not ____ combined.
e: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not chemically combined. Chemically is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They do not have well defined specific properties and the substances are not in fixed ____.
e: They do not have well defined specific properties and the substances are not in fixed ratios. Ratios is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mixtures may also be heterogeneous or ____.
e: The mixtures may also be heterogeneous or homogeneous. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution.

q: Therefore, the mixtures can be classified as two main categories: homogeneous and ____ mixtures.
e: Therefore, the mixtures can be classified as two main categories: homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts.

q: Apart from alloys containing two metals, solid-solid mixtures are ____.
e: Apart from alloys containing two metals, solid-solid mixtures are heterogeneous. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts.

q: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a ____.
e: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid ____ state.
e: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid crystalline state. Crystalline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Decantation is a process to separate ____.
e: Decantation is a process to separate mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is ____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is magnetic in nature. Magnetic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be ____.
e: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be separated. Separated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a ____ column.
e: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a fractionating column. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and ____ speed.
e: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and rotor speed. Rotor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chromatography is a separation method of the mixed substances that depends on the speed at which they move through special media, or chemical ____.
e: Chromatography is a separation method of the mixed substances that depends on the speed at which they move through special media, or chemical substances. Substances is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a ____).
e: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a gas). Gas is the idea that completes this fact.
